subject: MSA — Distinguishing direct vs indirect damages (lost revenue / data / goodwill)
messages:
From: Santosh Patel <santosh@acme.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA — Clarify damage carve-outs (lost profits, data loss, goodwill)

Grace — thanks for the draft MSA. A couple of items legal/procurement want clarified before we proceed to signature:

1) The current cap language is written as a single monetary cap with a carve-out for "certain" third-party claims. We need explicit treatment of: lost profits, loss of data (and cost to restore), and loss of goodwill/reputation.

2) Acme's stance: lost profits arising directly from Redwood's failure to deliver contracted capacity or from data deletion should be recoverable as direct damages (subject to a reasonable cap). Reputational harm/goodwill loss should usually be excluded as consequential.

Can you send us sample redline language that distinguishes these categories (i.e., examples we can circulate internally)? Also attach whatever precedence Redwood typically offers for enterprise Order Forms (caps tied to fees vs fixed buckets).

We'd like to keep the thread tight — copying procurement (Emma) for budget/thresholds.

Attachments: none on our side.

Thanks,
Santosh Patel
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
[santosh@acme.com]

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA — Clarify damage carve-outs (lost profits, data loss, goodwill)

Santosh — appreciate the clarity. Drafting notes and two short example snippets below (MSA-level and Order Form example). Attaching a marked-up MSA for context.

Attachment: Acme_MSA_Liability_Redline_v2.pdf (pdf) — redline of liability / cap sections

Proposed MSA snippet (short form):
"
Limitation of Liability. EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM (A) WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, AND (C) LOSSES ARISING FROM THE OTHER PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS DATA SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, NEITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR DIRECT DAMAGES ARISING UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO PROVIDER UNDER THE APPLICABLE ORDER FORM IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY, OR (II) TWO MILLION DOLLARS (US $2,000,000).

For clarity, "direct damages" includes reasonable, documented costs to restore or recreate Customer Data and proven lost revenue directly attributable to Provider's failure to perform obligations under this Agreement. Consequential, incidental, special, exemplary or punitive damages, including loss of goodwill, loss of brand value or loss of business opportunities, are excluded.
"

Order Form (customer-facing) — alternate cap: "
Aggregate liability for direct damages arising from incidents affecting production service shall be capped at the greater of (i) fees paid under the Order Form in the prior 12 months, or (ii) US $500,000 for Professional and Standard tiers, and US $2,000,000 for Enterprise tier. Direct damages specifically include costs to restore data and demonstrable lost revenue. Consequential damages (including reputational harm and loss of goodwill) are excluded.

Proposed next steps: Laura — can you confirm that the phrasing around "reasonable, documented costs to restore or recreate Customer Data" is sufficient evidence standard for us? Aditya — want to flag this to pricing (caps by tier).

Happy to hop on a quick call with Santosh + Emma if that would accelerate.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA — Clarify damage carve-outs (lost profits, data loss, goodwill)

Thanks Grace — that language is helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our side:

• On lost profits: we want the MSA to allow recovery of reasonably foreseeable lost profits that are the direct result of Redwood's failure to deliver/restore service (not speculative pipeline). Does the phrase "proven lost revenue directly attributable to Provider's failure to perform" map to that?

• On goodwill/reputation: Procurement will push to retain some recovery for reputational harm tied to specific contractual breaches (e.g., data exposure affecting key customers). Can Redwood consider a limited carve-in for reputational damages where a documented and demonstrable loss to a named customer is proven, subject to a separate per-event sub-cap?

If you can provide a one-paragraph redline we can circulate, we should be close.

Santosh
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: MSA — Clarify damage carve-outs (lost profits, data loss, goodwill)

Grace/Aditya — quick internal note before we send a formal redline back to Acme. Keeping in mind enforcement risk and precedential value across enterprise deals. My suggestions:

1) Lost profits: commit to recovery of "proven lost revenue" but limited to demonstrable, measurable revenue tied to the service outage (orders cancelled, lost subscriptions where we can show correlation). Avoid subjective measures (pipeline). Proposed language for insertion: 
"
For purposes of this Agreement, "proven lost revenue" means objectively documented, actual revenue lost by Customer as a direct result of Provider's material failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement, measured by Customer's closed sales, lost renewals or cancelled orders directly attributable to the outage and supported by contemporaneous records.
"

2) Data restoration costs: we should accept reasonable, documented costs to restore or recreate Customer Data as direct damages. Keep a cap tieback to fees (12 months) or the alternate fixed $ cap for enterprise. This preserves our operational exposure.

3) Reputational/goodwill: general exclusion remains. If Acme insists on a carve-in for reputational harm to a named customer, propose a narrow, per-event limited recovery: e.g., recoverable only where (i) Customer identifies the named third party prior to the event, (ii) the loss is documented by that third party (written claim or settlement), and (iii) recovery is subject to an additional sub-cap (e.g., $250,000 per event, aggregate not to exceed $500,000). This is a high bar but can be a compromise for strategic accounts.

I'll prepare a one-paragraph redline combining the above and send it to Grace to forward. Keep external messaging minimal — don't commit to $ figures before we align with pricing.

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_damages_snippets.txt (txt) — internal snippet & negotiation guidance

LAURA BENNETT
